components.text: Explain why temporal creaturely change would require intrinsic acquisition or loss in God's knowledge.
Whether temporal creaturely change requires God to acquire or lose knowledge and thereby change intrinsically.
Show that lacking alternative possibilities entails lacking the freedom relevant to perfect divine agency.
Whether inability to do otherwise is sufficient to show that a purely actual divine will is not perfectly free.
Whether difficult, unequal access to knowledge of God remains compatible with perfect divine love.
Whether difficult and unequal access to knowledge of God is compatible with God's revelatory purpose and perfect love.
Establish that the actuality grounding each dependent causal chain is one shared first cause of all such chains.
Whether the need for a first actualizer in each dependent causal chain establishes one shared first cause for all such chains.
Connect the causal ground reached by act-potency reasoning to a perfectly good and worship-worthy God.
Whether an actuality grounding causal dependence has thereby been identified as perfectly good and worthy of worship.
Explain why the scale, distribution, and apparent biological or moral uselessness of animal suffering is expected or justified.
Whether ordinary negligence standards apply straightforwardly to a transcendent creator who produces both potency and actuality.
Whether apparently gratuitous creaturely suffering licenses judging the transcendent creator defective or guilty of neglect.
Whether one eternal causal act avoids changing knowledge when propositions differ in truth across temporal locations.
Whether an eternal causal plan prevents temporal truth variation from requiring a relevant change in divine knowledge.
Whether the changing-knowledge objection depends specifically on presentism or temporal becoming understood presentistically.
Show why the sustaining source is one shared cause rather than a separate terminus for each dependent chain.
Connect continuous impartation of being to perfect goodness and worship-worthiness.
Whether continuous dependence identifies the sustaining cause as perfectly good and worthy of worship.
Whether multiple dependent beings or chains require one shared sustaining cause rather than several causes.
Explain why creator transcendence or human soul-building justifies immense prehuman suffering among nonmoral animals.
Whether the creator framework and human-directed redemptive goods answer immense suffering endured by nonmoral animals.
Explain how apparently gratuitous animal suffering can contribute to an ordered whole despite not building animal moral character.
Supply an alternative standard for judging whether evolutionary pain is gratuitous.
Whether animal suffering lacks justification when assessed through animal flourishing alone rather than ecosystemic and cosmic order.
Whether apparent biological or moral uselessness is sufficient to classify the aggregate suffering pattern as gratuitous.
Explain why widespread incompatible religious uptake is expected if God lovingly makes truth naturally and revelationally accessible.
Whether difficult but available natural and revealed knowledge adequately explains widespread incompatible religious traditions.
Explain why a perfectly loving God would permit nonuniform and non-overwhelming religious access among embodied persons.
Explain how epistemic distance can preserve a freely developing relationship rather than prevent relationship altogether.
Whether perfect love requires continuously unmistakable belief-enabling disclosure to every finite person.
Whether gradual and culturally mediated revelation explains persistent incompatible religious traditions.
